MASTER PROMPT — AI INTERVIEW AGENT WORKING PROTOTYPE

Build a fully functional web-based application called InterviewAI Agent.

The application is an AI-powered conversational technical interview platform designed to conduct realistic mock interviews based on a structured 31-day AI Cohort curriculum.

The goal is to create a working prototype, not just a UI mockup. All major features must be functional, connected, and testable.

  1. CORE OBJECTIVE

Create an AI Interview Agent that:

  • Conducts a conversational technical interview.

  • Uses the candidate's profile and curriculum knowledge.

  • Asks at least 8 questions during one interview.

  • Covers at least 4 different curriculum days.

  • Generates intelligent follow-up questions based on previous answers.

  • Maintains complete conversation context.

  • Evaluates technical knowledge, problem-solving ability, communication, and cultural/team-fit signals.

  • Provides structured feedback at the end.

  • Detects suspicious interview behavior using ethical anti-cheating/integrity signals.

  • Exposes the required HTTP API endpoint.

  • Allows interviews to be used either for practice or assessment.

The application should work even if no external database is available by providing a demo/mock-data mode.

  1. APPLICATION FLOW

Implement this flow:

Landing Page
→ Candidate Profile
→ Select Interview Type
→ Start Interview
→ AI Introduction
→ Question
→ Candidate Answer
→ AI Evaluation
→ Adaptive Follow-up
→ Next Topic
→ Minimum 8 Questions
→ Interview Completion
→ Performance Report
→ Recommendations

Interview types:

  1. Practice Interview

  2. Technical Assessment

  3. AI Cohort Evaluation

  1. CONVERSATIONAL & BEHAVIORAL REALISM

The AI interviewer must behave like a realistic human interviewer.

The interviewer should:

  • Introduce itself naturally.

  • Explain the interview rules.

  • Ask one question at a time.

  • Wait for the candidate's answer.

  • Understand incomplete answers.

  • Ask clarification questions when necessary.

  • Generate follow-up questions based on the previous answer.

  • Avoid repeatedly asking the same question.

  • Adjust question difficulty dynamically.

  • Maintain context throughout the interview.

  • Refer naturally to previous answers.

Example:

AI:
"Can you explain how a neural network learns?"

Candidate:
"It learns by changing the weights."

AI:
"Correct. You mentioned changing weights. Can you explain what role backpropagation plays in that process?"

The AI should NOT simply use a fixed list of questions.

Follow-up questions should depend on the candidate's responses.

Maintain an interview context object containing:

  • Candidate profile

  • Current curriculum day

  • Topics already covered

  • Questions asked

  • Candidate answers

  • Evaluation scores

  • Detected strengths

  • Detected weaknesses

  • Difficulty level

  • Remaining required questions

  1. INTERVIEW QUESTION REQUIREMENTS

Every completed interview MUST contain:

  • Minimum: 8 questions

  • Curriculum coverage: minimum 4 different days

  • At least 2 follow-up questions generated dynamically

  • At least 1 technical reasoning question

  • At least 1 practical/application question

  • At least 1 scenario-based question

  • At least 1 conceptual question

Question types:

  • Conceptual

  • Technical

  • Coding/problem solving

  • Scenario based

  • System/application design

  • Debugging

  • Behavioral/teamwork

  • Project-based

The system should track curriculum coverage.

Example:

Day 3 → Machine Learning Fundamentals
Day 7 → Neural Networks
Day 15 → LLMs
Day 22 → AI Agents

  1. ADVANCED ANTI-CHEATING & INTEGRITY MEASURES

Implement privacy-conscious integrity monitoring.

Do NOT secretly record or collect sensitive information.

Use transparent indicators such as:

  • Excessively long pauses

  • Repeated answer submission

  • Sudden answer-style changes

  • Copy/paste events where technically available

  • Multiple rapid tab/window changes where browser permissions allow

  • Unusually fast answers

  • Suspiciously identical answers

  • Answer consistency analysis

Display an integrity status:

  • Normal

  • Attention

  • Review Recommended

Do NOT automatically accuse a candidate of cheating.

Instead, show:

"Integrity signal detected. This does not prove misconduct. Review recommended."

For practice mode, integrity monitoring should be optional.

Do not use facial recognition, emotion recognition, biometric identification, or invasive surveillance.

Create an integrity event log:

{
"timestamp": "...",
"event_type": "tab_change",
"severity": "low",
"message": "Candidate changed browser focus."
}

  1. SKILL & CULTURE EVALUATION

Evaluate candidates across multiple dimensions.

Technical Skills:

  • Conceptual understanding

  • Technical accuracy

  • Problem solving

  • Application ability

  • Debugging/reasoning

Communication:

  • Clarity

  • Structure

  • Conciseness

  • Explanation quality

Behavioral:

  • Collaboration

  • Adaptability

  • Ownership

  • Critical thinking

  • Learning mindset

Culture/team-fit evaluation should NOT judge protected personal characteristics.

Evaluate only job-relevant behaviors such as:

  • Collaboration

  • Respectful communication

  • Adaptability

  • Feedback acceptance

  • Problem ownership

Generate scores from 0–100.

Example:

{
"technical_score": 82,
"problem_solving_score": 76,
"communication_score": 88,
"behavioral_score": 84,
"overall_score": 82
}

  1. CANDIDATE EXPERIENCE & FEEDBACK

After completing the interview, generate a detailed but easy-to-understand report.

Include:

Overall Score

Strengths

Example:

  • Strong understanding of machine learning fundamentals.

  • Good ability to explain technical concepts.

Areas for Improvement

Example:

  • Improve understanding of model evaluation.

  • Give more structured answers.

Question-by-Question Feedback

For each question:

  • Question

  • Candidate answer

  • Score

  • What was good

  • What could improve

  • Ideal answer points

  • Curriculum day

  • Skill assessed

Personalized Learning Plan

Recommend:

  • Curriculum days to revisit

  • Topics to practice

  • Suggested next interview difficulty

  • Practice missions

For Practice Mode, feedback should be encouraging and educational rather than punitive.

Implement an internal interviewer agent with the following behavior:

"You are InterviewAI, a professional technical interviewer.

Conduct a realistic conversational technical interview.

Ask one question at a time.

Use the candidate's profile and the 31-day curriculum.

Do not reveal the evaluation rubric during the interview.

Listen carefully to the candidate's answer.

Ask intelligent follow-up questions when the answer requires clarification or deeper reasoning.

Adapt question difficulty according to candidate performance.

Maintain complete conversation context.

Do not repeat questions.

Ensure at least 8 questions and coverage of at least 4 curriculum days.

Evaluate technical correctness, reasoning, communication and relevant behavioral competencies.

Remain professional, neutral and encouraging.

Do not make decisions based on protected characteristics.

At the end, generate structured evaluation data."

I have completed the InterviewAI Agent working prototype, fully implementing all functional specifications, backend Express API endpoints, 31-Day AI Cohort curriculum integration, adaptive interview engine, and rich UI components:

Key Highlights & Features Implemented:

  • 31-Day AI Cohort Syllabus: Integrated structured curriculum covering 6 core modules:

    1. AI Foundations & Math (Days 1–5)

    2. Classical Machine Learning (Days 6–10)

    3. Deep Learning & Computer Vision (Days 11–16)

    4. NLP, Large Language Models & Fine-Tuning (Days 17–21)

    5. Autonomous Agents, RAG & Vector Databases (Days 22–26)

    6. Production ML, AI Governance & Edge Deployment (Days 27–31)

  • Adaptive AI Interview Engine:

    • 8+ Question Sessions: Evaluates candidates across at least 4 distinct curriculum days.

    • Dynamic Follow-Ups: Probes candidate depth whenever brief or key-term dense responses are detected.

    • Archetype Rotation: Cycles through Conceptual, Technical, Coding, Scenario, System Design, Debugging, Behavioral, and Project-based question archetypes.

    • Server-side Gemini AI Integration & Demo Mode: Uses @google/genai on the server when GEMINI_API_KEY is present, with fallback to an intelligent rule-based engine in Demo Mode.

  • Ethical Anti-Cheating & Integrity Monitor:

    • Transparently logs focus switches/tab changes, paste events (>50 chars), and answer speed anomalies.

    • Provides non-accusatory status indicators (normal, attention, review_recommended).

  • Candidate Profile Manager:

    • View, edit, and create candidate profiles with cohort progress, completed missions, strong/weak topics, and historical attempt records.

  • Comprehensive Evaluation Report & Radar Charts:

    • Computes Overall Score (0-100) and sub-scores for Technical, Problem-Solving, Communication, and Behavioral competencies.

    • Renders Recharts competency radar chart, curriculum coverage bar chart, question-by-question breakdowns with ideal answer points, and a personalized learning plan.

  • Open REST API Contract & Interactive Sandbox:

    • Full API specification and live interactive testing interface for /api/v1/interview, /api/v1/candidate, and /api/v1/curriculum.

grading Ran quality control

I have resolved the runtime error (Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')).

Root Cause

Before initial data fetched from the API server, or when no candidates matched selectedCandidateId, the candidate lookups returned undefined. Components like Dashboard and CandidateProfileView attempted to access properties like .name directly on undefined, triggering the TypeError.

Changes Implemented

  • Defensive Candidate Fallbacks: Updated Dashboard.tsx and CandidateProfileView.tsx to provide fallback candidate objects and graceful empty state handling when candidates are loading or empty.

  • Safe Property Navigation: Added optional chaining and guards around candidate property accesses (e.g., currentCandidate?.name, currentCandidate?.learning_signals, completed_missions).

  • Synchronized Form State: Updated CandidateProfileView.tsx with useEffect state synchronization so form fields update cleanly whenever selected candidates change.

  • Dropdown Resilience: Updated Navbar.tsx candidate selector to display a loading fallback option while data resolves.
